officialTechnicalReferences.supports: Isolated/repeatable tests and explicit dependency seams; not hypothetical business rules.
Controllable time providers for deterministic time-dependent tests; relevant only to time cases.

findings.requirement: BIZQ-01 §4.1–4.3 requires understandable constraints, a meaningful choice, and feedback that explains the case decision.
findings.rationale: Every item has the literal constraint “The test must not use the live undefined.” It names no defined dependency or case fact. The shared mechanism/scenario feedback is also grammatically malformed across the unit, e.g. “while the real assembling a ... applies the rule” and “The test runs constructing ...”; it does not clearly explain the construction path.
findings.correction: Replace the undefined placeholder with the actual excluded dependency/source in each case, or remove it if redundant. Rewrite mechanismOrProperty and scenarioApplication as grammatical, case-specific explanations while keeping the established testability decision.

findings.requirement: BIZQ-01 §4.3 requires plausible alternatives and warns against systematic answer-form cues.
findings.rationale: The accepted choices repeatedly give a detailed “pass/supply/require [input] into assembly” recipe that directly matches the repeated stem prompt. Distractors often reduce to stubs, process-wide state, live dependencies, or post-construction patches. These are recognizable testing mistakes, but the repeated form leaves the key as the only complete per-instance path, making the answer pattern guessable before comparing the actual case boundary.
findings.correction: Keep the intended per-instance construction decision; revise the choice sets to provide credible competing approaches and case-specific failure reasons. Do not pad choices, equalize lengths, or impose a fixed count.
